Smart Reads of the Week: DBS vs OCBC vs UOB, 6.5% REIT Yields, Retirement Income, and AI Stocks
article:
Singapore stocks have had a cautious week, with the STI slipping on Tuesday before stabilising on Wednesday as local bank shares recovered slightly. Meanwhile, volatile bond markets and inflation concerns continue to put pressure on Asian banks.
With markets unsettled, investors are asking two important questions: which stocks offer value today, and which can provide dependable income for the years ahead?
This week’s Smart Reads compares DBS, OCBC and UOB, examines Temasek-backed REITs offering yields of around 6.5%, and explores whether Venture Corporation can sustain its dividends.
We also look at how CPF LIFE and dividend stocks can work together to provide S$3,000 a month in retirement, alongside opportunities in SGX dividend stocks and Singapore Exchange shares.
Finally, we compare Nvidia with AMD and discuss whether selling your losing stocks during a market dip is always the right decision.
Here are this week’s top articles:
DBS, OCBC and UOB: Which Singapore Bank Stock Is the Best Buy Now?
Singapore’s three major banks offer different strengths. We compare which presents the most attractive opportunity today.
Want S$3,000 a Month in Retirement? Here’s How CPF LIFE and Dividend Stocks Can Work Together
Discover how CPF LIFE and dividend income can complement each other to support your retirement goals.
3 Temasek-Backed Blue-Chip S-REITs Offering 6.5% Distribution Yields
These established REITs offer attractive yields, but what should income investors consider before buying?
Is Venture Corporation’s Cash-Rich Dividend Payout Plan Sustainable?
Venture’s strong cash position supports its dividends, but can the company maintain its payouts over time?
3 SGX Dividend Stocks to Watch as the STI Dips
Market weakness could create opportunities for income investors seeking quality businesses at more attractive valuations.
Nvidia vs AMD: Which Chip Stock Is the Better Buy Today?
Two AI chip leaders offer different growth prospects. We compare their profitability, valuations and investment potential.
SGX Shares Have Been a Big Winner: Is It Still a Buy Today?
Singapore Exchange shares have enjoyed a strong run. We examine whether there is still room for further gains.
Should You Sell Your Losers When the Market Dips?
Selling a losing stock can feel sensible, but the right decision depends on more than its share price.
